title: Disable system sleep on the DGX Spark
head: b7172acee467
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Unreadable or absent DMI fields silently classify a Spark as non-Spark
leads.consequence: If either DMI file is absent or unreadable even on a DGX Spark, the helper returns failure with cat's diagnostic suppressed. The installer quietly leaves sleep enabled, both menu guards evaluate ! omarchy-hw-dgx-spark to true (provided their other guards pass), and the migration exits successfully and receives a completed marker. A later DMI recovery alone will not cause that migration to run again. The new test replaces the detector with a stub, so it does not exercise this case.
leads.triage: factual mechanism overlaps Opus Q1 missing-file cases; trigger speculative

leads.summary: An existing but incomplete DGX drop-in is accepted as successful migration
leads.consequence: If an interrupted or failed direct write leaves an empty/truncated omarchy-dgx-spark.conf, the next migration sees -f and exits 0 without checking [Sleep] and the four no settings. omarchy-migrate then marks migration complete. This can leave some or all of the sleep paths enabled indefinitely on that Spark until the hardware installer is run again or the file is repaired by hand. Check content or replace atomically rather than using mere existence as a success marker.

limits: The absent-DMI finding is conditional: there is no evidence that normal DGX Spark firmware actually omits either DMI file. A plain trailing newline is stripped by bash command substitution and accepted; surrounding spaces are not.

Did not execute installation against actual /etc, the migration with sudo, systemctl, logind, or the host's DMI. The migration's preexisting-file case follows from pinned source inspection, not a simulated privileged migration.

review.py head shell test ran successfully: plan/runs/20260927T084159Z-b4144a2b (exit 0). An attempted menu-guards-test run in plan/runs/20260927T084159Z-5dec113a failed solely because the deliberately scoped snapshot excluded shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js, so it is not evidence of a PR regression; both sealed runs verified.

Read-only related-open-PR file queries: #12125 adds a different 10-omarchy-suspend-then-hibernate.conf plus logind lid policy; #12723 adds another run_logged entry in install/hardware/all.sh; #12826 adds an alias to system.suspend; #12255 changes menu override merge and uses an independent synthetic hibernate guard. These require ordinary diff integration if merged, but inspected patches show no pinned-head conflicting ID, shared output target, or confirmed test failure.

flags.claim: The detector requires sys_vendor to be NVIDIA, so OEM GB10 systems (for example ASUS Ascent GX10 or Lenovo ThinkStation PGX) are not matched.
flags.why: Stated as fact, but the OEM units' raw DMI values were not verified. The only evidence is a third-party README (KPFstudio/gb10-monitor) that shows display strings ('LENOVO · ThinkStation PGX', 'ASUSTeK · GX10'), not raw sys_vendor/product_name. The final report keeps this as hypothesis H2. The helper's own logic is verified: it needs sys_vendor == NVIDIA AND product_name == NVIDIA_DGX_Spark (sandbox cases helper-dmi-oem-lenovo and helper-dmi-oem-asus with those strings exit 1).

flags.claim: omarchy toggle suspend -> flips suspend-off, notifies "Suspend now available in system menu"
flags.why: Lost qualifier. The command notifies 'Suspend now available in system menu' only on the toggle that clears suspend-off. From the default state, the first run sets suspend-off and notifies 'Suspend removed from system menu', which is true on a Spark. My final report (F2) has the same missing qualifier.

flags.claim: Two nearby commands still describe the hidden rows as available (line 5); heading: 'omarchy toggle suspend and omarchy hibernation setup still offer the hidden rows on a Spark' (line 16).
flags.why: True for omarchy-toggle-suspend (with the C12 qualifier). omarchy-hibernation-setup never mentions the menu or a row. It asks 'Use <size> on boot drive to make hibernation available?' (line 81) and 'Reboot to enable hibernation?' (line 164). It is the manual (manual/36-system-sleep.md:21), not the command, that says the Hibernate option appears. Neither command 'offers the rows'. My final report (F2) uses similar wording.

flags.claim: Gate the two rows on the sleep policy ..., for example [[ ! -e /etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/omarchy-dgx-spark.conf ]] or logind's CanSuspend/CanHibernate, so the menu follows what is in force.
flags.why: 'Follows what is in force' holds for CanSuspend/CanHibernate. The file check follows only Omarchy's own drop-in: it would not notice a user drop-in that sorts later and sets AllowSuspend=yes, or any other policy. Also missing a caveat: gating on CanSuspend changes non-Spark behaviour, because logind answers 'na' or 'no' wherever the kernel or config does not support sleep, which the current rows ignore. The suggestion is otherwise sound and matches the final report.

flags.claim: the menu hides Suspend and Hibernate only on a Spark
flags.why: Read literally, this is not so: on non-Spark machines the rows are still hidden when suspend-off is set or hibernation is unavailable (guards-matrix.tsv, head rows with spark=0). The intended meaning, that the new check hides them only on a Spark, is correct. My final report uses the same phrasing.

flags.claim: menu-guards-test.sh evaluates when strings with stub commands.
flags.why: menu-guards-test.sh evaluates one shipped `when` (update.themes) in bash against fixture HOMEs using the real repo commands (the stub git is only on the updater's PATH), and it evaluates `checked` expressions with a stubbed omarchy-dns function. The point stands (guard expressions evaluated in bash against fixtures and stubs), but 'when strings with stub commands' is slightly inexact.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

One issue found in the tested scope: two nearby commands and the manual still act as if suspend and hibernation can be turned on on a Spark. There is also an optional test improvement, because the new test lets several regressions through.

**Verified:** The drop-in turns off every systemd sleep operation, the new menu check hides Suspend and Hibernate only on a Spark, and the install script and migration behave correctly on Spark and non-Spark machines.

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Drop-in (systemd v261 source) | All four `Allow*=no` keys cover every sleep operation. logind reports `CanSuspend`/`CanHibernate` as `no` and refuses the Suspend, Hibernate and Sleep calls and the sleep key, lid and idle actions. `sleep.conf.d` is re-read on every check, so no reload is needed. |
| Menu guards (production `guardScript`, 8 combinations of suspend-off × hibernation available × Spark) | Suspend shows only when suspend is not toggled off and the machine is not a Spark. Hibernate shows only when hibernation is available and the machine is not a Spark. Every non-Spark combination matches the base branch. |
| Detector (synthetic DMI directory) | Matches `NVIDIA` / `NVIDIA_DGX_Spark` with or without a trailing newline. Exits 1 with no stderr for missing or unreadable files and for near-miss values. The strings match DMI output quoted in two public DGX Spark forum reports. |
| Install script | On a Spark it writes exactly `[Sleep]` plus the four lines, and a rerun leaves the file unchanged. On other machines it creates no directory. |
| Migration (`/etc` redirected, `sudo` stubbed) | Non-Spark: no `sudo` call. Spark without the file: one `sudo bash .../nvidia-dgx-spark.sh`. File present: skipped. `sudo` failure: exits nonzero, so the migration stays pending. |
| Tests | The new test passes on head and fails on base. `menu-test.sh`, `menu-guards-test.sh`, `bin-style-test.sh` and `test/cli` pass on head and base. |

### `omarchy toggle suspend`, `omarchy hibernation setup` and the manual still act as if sleep can be turned on on a Spark

On a Spark, the rows are hidden whatever the toggles or hibernation setup say:

```text
omarchy toggle suspend      -> flips suspend-off; when it turns suspend back on,
                               notifies "Suspend now available in system menu"
                               -> Suspend row stays hidden (! omarchy-hw-dgx-spark)
omarchy hibernation setup   -> offers "Use <RAM size> on boot drive to make hibernation available?"
                               -> creates a swapfile the size of physical RAM
                               -> Hibernate row stays hidden, AllowHibernation=no
```

`manual/36-system-sleep.md` still says the toggle "reveals/hides the option" and that the Hibernate option appears once hibernation is set up. The new manual sentence also does not say how to turn sleep back on. Because the rows are gated on the hardware rather than on the sleep policy, removing the drop-in turns sleep back on in logind, but the menu still hides both rows. The hibernation path assumes `omarchy-hibernation-setup` gets past its early exits on the Spark's kernel (for example the `/sys/power/image_size` check), which was not checked.

**Impact:** When a Spark user turns suspend back on, or follows the manual, the message does not match the menu. `omarchy hibernation setup` can spend a large amount of disk space (the size of physical RAM) on hibernation that stays disallowed.

**Suggested change:** Gate the two rows on the sleep policy instead of the hardware, for example `[[ ! -e /etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/omarchy-dgx-spark.conf ]]` or logind's `CanSuspend`/`CanHibernate`, so the menu follows the sleep policy. The file check follows only this drop-in. `CanSuspend`/`CanHibernate` reflect every sleep setting, but they would also change which rows show on other machines. Other options are to make `omarchy-toggle-suspend` and `omarchy-hibernation-setup` Spark-aware, or to add a sentence to the manual.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/dgx-spark-hardware-test.sh` replaces the detector with a shell function and only greps the menu text. Each of these changes, applied alone to a copy of the head, still passed the test. Removing `AllowHybridSleep=no` from the install script failed it, as it should.

| Change to a copy of the head | New test |
|---|---|
| Suspend `when` uses `\|\| ! omarchy-hw-dgx-spark` (Suspend then shows on a Spark) | passes |
| Detector compares against a product name that never matches | passes |
| The `nvidia-dgx-spark.sh` line removed from `install/hardware/all.sh` | passes |
| `migrations/1790364978.sh` deleted | passes |

`xps13-sidecar-amps-test.sh` already covers the same ground for its hardware. It runs the real detector through a DMI env override, checks the `all.sh` wiring, and runs the migration with `sudo` stubbed. `menu-guards-test.sh` evaluates guard expressions in bash against fixtures and stubs. The same approach would need a DMI path override in `omarchy-hw-dgx-spark` (for example `${OMARCHY_DMI_PATH:-/sys/class/dmi/id}`).

**Not confirmed on hardware:** The PR reports the logind result with the drop-in in place. It does not report running the detector on the Spark, and the menu was not checked. Running `omarchy-hw-dgx-spark && echo match` on the Spark and opening the System menu once would settle both. The detector requires `sys_vendor` to be `NVIDIA` and `product_name` to be `NVIDIA_DGX_Spark`, so OEM GB10 systems (for example ASUS Ascent GX10 or Lenovo ThinkStation PGX) that report their own vendor or product name would not be matched. Whether they should be is a scope decision.

**Related open PR:** #12826 changes the same `system.suspend` menu line on `quattro`, so a small textual conflict is likely when the branches meet.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `b7172ac` against base `dragon`, plus upstream systemd v261 and Linux DMI sysfs source. Sandboxed runs used a synthetic DMI directory, stub commands, a stubbed `sudo` and redirected `/etc` paths. The menu guards were evaluated with `bash -c` rather than the production `bash -lc`. Real logind, `systemd-sleep`, `sudo`, the running menu and DGX Spark hardware were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
